qualification: Pre-fix index_fragments walked moof children only for traf boxes, completely ignoring mfhd (accepting missing mfhd, duplicate mfhd, overlong 12-byte mfhd, and zero sequence_number), while fragment_defaults accepted trex boxes with track_ID == 0 or duplicate track_ID entries (silently shadowing later trex defaults via find()). Pre-fix baseline passed 3/3 controls and both forced acceptance gates failed because all 6 malformed cases indexed and reached native VP9 playback.

Validating a mandatory singleton version-0 8-byte mfhd with non-zero sequence_number in every moof and non-zero unique track_ID values in mvex/trex refuses all 6 malformed cases as Error::Invalid before publishing samples or admitting native decoders.

All 4 healthy controls (regular MP4, single-fragment fMP4, three-fragment sequential fMP4, and distinct multi-track trex entries) retain exact coded packets, sync flags, 50 Hz clocks, sample/packet budgets, analytic 16x16 VP9 planes/RGB (128/130), 32 total public clamped seek targets, rewind, and repeated EOF.
4 focused tests, 74 related MP4/HLS/VP9 integration tests, 17 MP4 unit tests, 35 minimal-configuration (--no-default-features) tests, offline fixture generator unittest, and full player build pass.

ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015, 8.8.3, 8.8.4, and 8.8.5 specify unique non-zero trex track IDs and a mandatory singleton mfhd box per moof with a positive 1-based sequence_number. All fixtures are pure synthetic offline VP9/fMP4 files requiring neither FFmpeg nor network access.
counting: One fragmented MP4 mfhd header and trex track-ID integrity fix (FVID-0183). No extra IDs for individual mfhd/trex variants, controls, or fixture generator.
